lines.text: Village 07. A dozen lanterns, one well, and one rule.
Never cross the boundary. Those who leave are never seen again.
Tobin left last winter. Nobody says his name anymore.
You haven't slept in days. Under the floorboards, something hums. Low. Patient.
The village is waking. Maybe Mayor Orrin is, too.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Up before the roosters? You and me both, friend. Bad dreams, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Whatever keeps you up, the rule still stands. We stay inside the boundary. The Warden keeps us safe.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Tobin didn't stay.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Tobin made his choice. Let him rest, and leave his things where they lie.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Still chasing Tobin's ghosts? I can see it on you. He had the same look.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Ghosts are poor company. Go home and sleep. The hum stops if you stop listening.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: So you hear it too.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: ...Good day, friend.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Tobin's pages. His map. That stone. Where did you... no. I know where.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Everyone who ever left carried things like those. Every one. Not one came back.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Burn them, friend. Tonight. Before the Warden notices what you're carrying.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Go while the lanterns are low. I'll tell them I never saw you.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: And if you find it... no. Don't send word. Just keep walking.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: No smoke from your chimney yet, friend.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: ...I'll pretend I didn't notice. Just this once.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Keep to the lanterns, friend.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: The Warden watches over all of us. It always has.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Paradise. Tobin said it just like that. Like a prayer.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: The Warden told me once: keep them in, keep them safe. But I dream of steel stairs, too.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: The light runs thinnest at the old bridge, south. Watch for the flicker.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Take this. I won't watch another one leave empty-handed.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Good. Good. You don't know what it means to hear that.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: Burn them in your own hearth, not the square. And stay well clear of the old bridge.

lines.speaker: Mayor Orrin
lines.text: The light's gone thin there lately. It gives people ideas.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Couldn't sleep either? Nobody does, not really. Not here.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: I dream of stairs. Metal ones, going down and down. The floor hums like a cat.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Orrin walks at this hour too. Go keep him company.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: That's Tobin's book. Does he write about the stairs?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: He writes about Paradise.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Hm. In my dream there's a door at the bottom. A number painted on it. Zero... one.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Tobin used to sit under the orange tree by the blue house, writing. Scratch, scratch.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Said he had to put the dream down before it faded.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: What dream?

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Same as mine, child. Same as everyone's. We just don't say.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: The water's been strange all week. Look too long and it looks back.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Orrin's pacing his porch again. He only does that when someone means to leave.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Going, are you? Don't fuss. Tobin had that same walk.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: If you find the stairs, child, go all the way down. I always wake before the bottom.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Stairs, and a hum, and a door. Every night the same.

lines.speaker: Old Tamsin
lines.text: Hm. Mind the well, child. It's deeper than it looks.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Sun's barely up and you're underfoot. What.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Couldn't sleep.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Nobody sleeps right round here. Soil does. Never floods, never fails. Not natural, if you ask me.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: What's that in your pocket? It's buzzing like a wasp in a jar.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Tobin dug round that pink tree for weeks. Now I know why. Get it off my field.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Tobin? Helped in my fields. Good hands. Head in the clouds.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Kept staring at that pink tree, east side. Like it was humming him a song.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Then one night, gone. Left a row half-dug. Who does that?

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Mayor's gone the colour of a turnip. That your doing?

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Found a bolt in my furrow once. Clean steel, not a speck of rust. Dirt here's... wrong.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Off somewhere? Huh. Tobin had that look, last I saw him.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Go round my field, not through it. And... mind yourself out there.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Beans won't hoe themselves.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Go on. Shoo.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Oh! You gave me a fright. Stall's not open yet, love.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Talk to the Mayor first, dear. He likes to see the sleepless ones before anyone else.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Tobin used to come by your stall, didn't he?

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Every market day. Bought nothing. Asked about everything.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: He left this with me. Said it was for anyone who ever asked about Paradise.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: You've got that look, dear. Take it, quick, before I lose my nerve.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: The Mayor came asking what I'd sold you. Turnips, I said. Turnips!

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Go and talk to him, dear, before he worries himself sick.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Off for a walk? Don't tell me where. I'm a terrible liar, dear.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Tobin never bought a thing, but I'd have given him anything. Same goes for you.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Keep that map folded, love. The Mayor notices paper like a hawk notices mice.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Tobin drew it in my back room. Said the humming told him where to put the lines.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Turnips, thread, lamp oil. Nothing you need today, dear.

lines.speaker: Hessa
lines.text: Come back on market day. I'll save you the good thread.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: You're awake too! I'm counting lanterns. There's twelve. There's always twelve.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Mum says don't count the wall. You can't count a wall anyway. I tried.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The blue wall at the bridge blinks when the lanterns go out! I counted!

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: It did it the night Tobin went away. One, two... blink! Mum says I dreamed it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Did you?

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: No! I'm the best counter in Village 07.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Are you in trouble? The Mayor's doing his angry eyebrows.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: When Tobin was in trouble, he went and looked at the blue wall. For ages.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: It's blinking right now! Lanterns out, wall out! I'll count for you!

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: One... two... GO! That's how Tobin did it. I saw. I never told anyone.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Twelve lanterns. Thirteen if you count the moon. I don't.

lines.speaker: Pip

You blink. Sky again. Clouds. Your own tired face.
Just water. Just sky.

Your home. The quilt, the kettle, the chair by the window.

lines.text: Stop. Don't step there. That grey isn't dirt. It's what's left after dirt gives up.

lines.text: Another sleepless one, walking south with a humming pocket. Which village? One with a bridge?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Village 07.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Mira, Village 12. I chart the green line, where living land ends. It moves a little every year.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: A drone spooked me and my satchel went into the toxic pools. Fetch it? I'll owe you a theory.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: My satchel! Did you look inside? Of course you did. I would have.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: That crystal's grid rearranges itself. Near your shard it moves faster. Why, do you suppose?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Keep the two together. I want to watch. And I want to see the dead city south of here.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Lead on. Someone ought to take notes on your terrible ideas.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The satchel? Still in the pools, unless it learned to swim. Leather doesn't. I checked.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Mind the fumes. If your head starts to swim, drink water. And stay out of the drones' light.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: They won't hurt you. They'll just walk you back to where you started. Politely. Endlessly.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Mind the grey. It's hungrier than it looks.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: And if a drone finds you, don't run. It only makes the lecture longer.
A leather satchel, half-sunk in green muck. Inside, wrapped in a scarf, lies a clear crystal.
A fine grid is etched through its heart. As your shard draws near, the lines slide and rearrange.
The shard's hum climbs to meet it, like two voices finding the same note.
An old stone milestone. Fresh paint marks run down its side, each with a year scratched beside it.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The last two marks are mine. The rest were already here. Someone's measured this for decades.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Each mark is where the grass gave up that year. And each one sits a step further south.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The green line isn't shrinking. It's growing. Nobody back home believes me.
An old stone milestone. Fresh paint marks run down its side, each with a year scratched beside it.
The oldest marks sit nearest the village. Each newer one is a step further south.
Someone is measuring the edge of the green. And year by year, the green is winning.
The paint marks march south down the milestone, year after year. Slowly. Stubbornly.
Wherever the green line is going, it isn't going back.
A dead tree at the edge of the green, its bark split like old paper.
In the cracks, fine black threads twitch. Not roots. Not fungus. They move in neat little rows.
Rot is never this tidy. Something is eating this tree on purpose.
The black threads are still at work inside the bark.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Don't touch it. I've watched them take a tree a week. They always come from the south.
The black threads go still where you look. As if they're waiting for you to leave.
On the village side of the trunk, the grass grows green right up to the roots.
A small Warden outpost, white paint flaking. A dusty screen flickers awake as you lean close.

lines.speaker: THE WARDEN
lines.text: RESIDENTS RETURNED THIS CYCLE: 1,207. INJURIES: 0.

lines.speaker: THE WARDEN
lines.text: Resident. You are outside safe territory. Please return home. You are missed.
Twelve hundred returned, not one of them hurt. Yet you've never heard of anyone coming back.

lines.speaker: THE WARDEN
lines.text: RESIDENT. YOU ARE OUTSIDE SAFE TERRITORY.
The screen dims again. It sounds less like an order than a worry.
A rusted wreck, its roof peeled back like the lid of a tin.
Wedged inside is a Warden drone, its white shell torn open by dozens of tiny claws.
Its arms are still folded around a child's leather boot. Whatever it was guarding, it held on.
The torn drone is still in the wreck, still holding on.
Whatever clawed it open came from the south. You don't have the heart to move it.
The road ends in a city. Or in what a city leaves behind once it stops.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: No green line here at all. Nothing left to measure. That's a first.
Somewhere in the ruins, metal rings on metal. A shout. Then something chitters back.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Someone's fighting. We can be heroes or witnesses. I've never enjoyed witnessing.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Down! No, too late, you're in it now. Here!
A fighter in a red scarf shoves a length of rebar into your hands. The rubble starts to chitter.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Crawlers. Swing when they jump. Don't stop till they stop.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Not bad. You swing like a farmer, but they stopped jumping.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Kael. Been out here a year, fighting the swarm alone. It gets old.
He lifts a medallion from his neck. It hums against your shard, a note you feel in your teeth.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Woke up wearing it. Can't remember getting it. You hold it. I'll hold the line.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: There are others in these ruins. I've seen their fires. Let's go knock.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Less talking!

lines.speaker: Kael

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You! Don't just stand there. Here, take this!

lines.text: Shh. You'll wake them. The crawlers sleep in the rubble when it's quiet.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Someone's fighting near the old square. He needs you more than I do right now.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Go. Come back after. I'll be here, I promise.

lines.speaker: Nova

Her hands are warm. The ache drains out of you like a tide going out.

lines.speaker: Nova

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Round two! Or three. I lost count. The rig didn't.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Match the waves, lock them in. Easy. Ish.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Everyone's here! Six artifacts, six people, one very nervous rig.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Each piece hums its own note. Match the waves two at a time, then lock them in.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Get it right and they'll sing together. Get it wrong and, well. Let's get it right.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Whoa, hi, hello, don't touch that. Or that. Definitely not that.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: There's a fight by the square and I'm an engineer, not a hero. You look like a hero. Ish.

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: So, find the rest of us. I'll keep the solder warm.

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Lovely. Terrifying. Mostly terrifying.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Busy! Talking to wires. They're shy.

lines.speaker: Ryn

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Six of us. Six artifacts. One heading. I don't believe in coincidence.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I believe in design. Which raises the question: whose?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: That wall isn't weather. Weather doesn't stand perfectly still for a hundred years.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: And Eli walks a step ahead of us, like a man who already knows the way. I'm writing that down.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Made, not born. I keep turning it over like a specimen. It doesn't help.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I've checked his card eleven times. Still says 01. Still doesn't explain anything.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The crystal's grid has stopped pointing east. It points down. Right under our feet.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Paradise was an address. With a basement.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Look at the crystal. Now look at that corridor. And that one. And the stairs.
The etched grid matches the silo line for line: every hall, every turn, the spiral of the stairs.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: It isn't a crystal. It's a floor plan of this place. Somebody gave me directions home.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Ten thousand people, and every one of them has a question for us. Now I know how it feels.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I want to read everything down here. Twice. Then argue with it.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: If I go into that chamber, I come out someone else. Or someone I used to be.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I can't decide which frightens me more. Let's go before I do.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The school map. I traced the green line on it when I was six. I've been tracing it ever since.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Now the swarm is tracing us. To the core. Let's choose before it chooses for us.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: We'll forget all of it. The map, the line, you. I'm writing it down anyway. Habit.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Maybe one day somebody finds my notes and thinks I was mad. I hope so.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Three relays, and every Warden on the surface hears us. For once, let's be loud.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: If this works, the green line won't creep any more. It'll run.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The green line ends a little further out every year. Out here, that's practically a miracle.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I'd like to meet whoever's doing it. I have questions. Several hundred.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: That medallion. Turn it over.
Scratched into the back, worn almost smooth: HOLD THE DOOR.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Had it as long as I remember. Never found the door. Figure I'll know it when I see it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Crawlers go for the ankles. Swing low. Or grow taller.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Swing when they jump. Rest when they don't. Simple.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Your quiet friend. Eli. Never seen him eat. Never seen him sleep.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Not saying anything. Just saying I notice who doesn't eat.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Big wall. Glowing door. In my experience, the nicer the door, the worse the room.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Eli wants to go first. I don't like it. Nobody goes first but me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: He walked in first. That was supposed to be me. It's always supposed to be me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Made or born, it doesn't matter. He bled for us. Silver counts.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Medallion's warm. HOLD THE DOOR. If there's a door in all this ash, it's here somewhere.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Stay off the open street. Whatever tore Eli open didn't leave.
Kael stops at the guard post by the hatch stairs. His fingers find the keypad without looking.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Four, one, one, seven. I knew it before I saw it. How do I know that?
The keypad blinks green. Below it hangs an empty hook, worn smooth, just the size of his medallion.
Kael stops dead at the guard post by the hatch stairs. His fingers find the keypad without looking.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Four, one, one, seven. My code. My post. I remember standing right here, every night.
Below the keypad hangs an empty hook, worn smooth, just the size of his medallion.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Ten thousand people, one hatch, nowhere to run. Good thing I'm not the running kind.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Read your screens. I'll watch the stairs.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Go in, come out remembering. Fine. I just hope I like who I was.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: If I don't, I'll start over. Did it once already, apparently.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Security tag. I stood at that hatch six years. Then they carried me up and I forgot the door.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: HOLD THE DOOR. I scratched that on the back myself. Turns out I meant it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Burn them. I'll stand at the furnace door. Nothing gets past while you do it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: And if I forget all this... tell me anyway. Somebody tell me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: A relay's just a door with no walls. Stand in the ring. Swing when they jump.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I'll take the left. You hold the middle. Don't you dare fall.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Eyes up. Stay close.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: If something has to bleed today, it's me first. Not up for discussion.
The radio crackles: the same lullaby as always. Nova hums along under her breath.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: It only ever plays this song. I knew the words before I ever heard it. Isn't that strange?
You know the next note before she sings it. You have never heard it in your life.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Then someone sang it to both of us. Somewhere warm, with a low ceiling and a soft hum.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: If the air starts tasting sweet, drink water. Sweet means poison out here.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: And if you fall, I'll be there. I think that's what I'm for.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Eli sat up with me last night. He didn't sleep. I don't think he ever does.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: I asked if he was tired. He said he'd forgotten how, and smiled like it was a joke.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Eli says he'll go in first. He said it like he decided a long time ago.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: I asked if he was afraid. He said he'd forgotten how. He didn't smile this time.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: I couldn't find a pulse. Now I keep checking my own, to be sure I still know how.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Silver or not, he hurt. I saw it. That makes him one of us.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: The air tastes sweet in here. Drink water. Please. I can't lose anyone else today.
Her radio hisses, then catches the lullaby, louder than you've ever heard it. As if it's close.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Listen. The speakers on the walls. They crackle exactly like my radio.
She holds the radio up to a speaker grille. The two hiss in perfect time, like an echo.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: My radio was never catching a station. It was catching this place.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: They bake bread down here. That's what we smelled at the sinkhole. Bread, from underground.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Everyone's so pale, and so happy to see us. I don't know what to do with my hands.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Dr. Hale says it'll hurt. I'll hold your hand. You hold mine.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Whatever we were, we'll still be us afterwards. I'm almost sure.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Lights out, every night, the lullaby on every speaker. My mother sang along, off-key.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: I remember her now. I'm not losing her twice. Let's go.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: I'll forget the song. Then one night I'll hear it and cry, and not know why.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: That's all right. Crying means some part of you remembers.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Go, hold the rings. If you fall, I'll be there. That's still what I'm for.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Use your supplies. Being brave isn't the same as being careless.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Hold still... there. You'll be fine. You're tougher than you look.
She hums a few notes of the lullaby, then stops, frowning, as if she's lost the thread.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Fun fact: that core was stone-cold when I found it. Dead as a doorknob. Deader.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Now it pulses every eleven seconds. Scary part? It isn't listening. It's sending.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Sending to who?

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Great question. Love it. Hate it. Mostly hate it.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Rig's built, wired and only slightly on fire. It needs all six pieces humming at once.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: So, find the others. I'll keep talking to the wiring. It likes me.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Those coordinates point dead east. Into the white. I checked three times, then once for luck.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Luck said the same thing. Rude.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: The core's going wild. Every pulse points at that arch. Like a dog at its own front door.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: That's a metaphor. I hope. I really, really hope.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: It's the Wardens. It has to be. Because if it isn't, I don't know what's in there.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Eli fixed my rig once, you know. Never said how he knew where the wires went.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: This street hums. Not the core: the street. Something big is running underneath it.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Find the way down. I'll be over here, being brave quietly.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Up top, the core pulsed every eleven seconds. Down here? Every two. And getting faster.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: It isn't warming up because it's home. It's warming up because it's nearly done sending.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Done sending what?

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Ask me something easier. Please.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Up top, the core pulsed every eleven seconds. Down here it went every two. Faster and faster.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: It wasn't warming up because it was home. It was counting down. And I carried it the whole way.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Their air scrubbers are older than my grandmother's grandmother. And gorgeous. Look at the welds!

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Sorry. You were saying something about the fate of humanity. Go on.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Memory chamber. It's basically a rig for heads. I'm in. I'm scared, but I'm in.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: If I come out boring, you have permission to put me back.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: I was the kid who carried the spare seed. And I brought one back, wired up for the enemy.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Core. Now. Either we burn my core, or I teach it some manners.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Furnace. Right. Goodbye, little core. I really liked you. That was the whole problem.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Go on. Before I start naming it.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Three relays, three rings. Hold each one until it locks. I'll start writing the patch.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: A patch for a swarm. In a basement. During an alarm. Best day of my life.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: All three singing! Get me to the core. I've got a swarm to argue with.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: And this time, I win.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Don't mind me. Talking to the wiring. It listens better than people.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Present company excluded. Mostly.
Eli's palm is cut open, a clean line from a rusted fence. Not one drop of blood.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: It's nothing.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: It isn't bleeding.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Then it really is nothing. Walk on, seeker.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Eat your ration. I already ate.
You never saw him eat. Come to think of it, you've never seen his pack open.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: When we reach the white, let me walk in first. I know the way in.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: I wish I didn't.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: When we reach the arch, I go first. Kael will argue. Let him. I'll still go.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Seeker. Whatever I find in there, keep them walking. Keep them together.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Keep walking, seeker. You're closer than you think.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: To what? To everything.
You wake in the grass, aching. The poison has gone from your blood. Someone carried you here.
Overhead, something white hums away over the trees, unhurried.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: You went down like a sack of meal. Fascinating. Please don't repeat the experiment.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Drink water before the air does that to you again.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Breathe. Good. You're back.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The city wants us dead, so let's be contrary and stay alive.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Shh, easy. You're all right. I've got you.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Breathe with me. In... and out. There. Let's not do that again.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Still breathing? Good. Saves me digging.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Swing sooner next time.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Easy. You went down hard. The ash out here is worse than the city's.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Drink something. Then we keep going. Together.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: There you are. Stay with me. The swarm doesn't get you. Not today.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Up you get. Ten thousand people need us standing.
You wake, aching, at the last safe place you passed.
The shard is still humming. So, somehow, are you.
East of the city, the land ends in a wall of white, taller than any sky should allow.
It doesn't drift like cloud. It breathes.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Wait here. I'll scout ahead. Whatever you hear, wait for me.
He walks into the white without looking back. You think of his hand, and the cut that never bled.
East of the city, the land ends in a wall of white, taller than any sky should allow.
It doesn't drift like cloud. It breathes.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Wait here. I'll scout ahead. Whatever you hear, wait for me.
He walks into the white without looking back. For the first time, your shard falls silent.
The ash plain runs flat and grey for miles. Nothing grows. Nothing hums. Even the wind sounds tired.
Then the world ends in white: a wall of cloud taller than any sky should allow. It breathes.
At its foot glows a stone arch, warm as a hearth. Carved across the top, one word: PARADISE.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Coordinates say right there. The core says right there. Everything says right there. I hate it.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Stay close to me now. All of you. We are nearly there.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Stop here. All of you.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: I'm going in first. Alone. If it's safe, I'll call.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Not a chance. If anyone walks in first, it's me.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Not this time, Kael. You know how to walk in. I know how to walk back out.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: And if you don't call?

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: Then you'll know. Wait for me, seeker. Whatever you hear.
The arch glows. The white beyond it doesn't move.
For a moment you think someone inside is calling your name. Nobody is.
Eli staggers out of the white and falls to his knees. Something runs between his fingers.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: There is no Paradise. Don't go inside. Please...
His palm. The cut that never bled. It's bleeding now: silver, bright as mercury, like moonlight.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: I was made to walk with you. To keep you safe. Never by force. I'm sorry I couldn't...

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Let me... no. No pulse. There's no pulse. I don't think there ever was one.
Eli staggers out of the white and falls to his knees. Something runs between his fingers.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: There is no Paradise. Don't go inside. Please...
Nova presses the wound. It isn't blood. It's silver, bright as mercury, and it won't stop.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: I was made to walk with you. To keep you safe. Never by force. I'm sorry I couldn't...

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Let me... no. No pulse. There's no pulse. I don't think there ever was one.
Where Eli lay there is only silver dust, lifting on no wind, drifting back into the white.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Silver. No pulse. Made, not born. Someone built him, and built him to care about us. Who?

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: It's the Wardens. They'd say anything to keep us out. Even through him.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Made or born, he walked in first. For us. I'm not letting that be for nothing.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: His card. 01. I'll keep it. He said doors remember. Let's find out if one does.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: We go in. All of us. For him.
A stone arch, older than the ash, glowing softly from within. Carved across the top: PARADISE.
After the word, a row of empty bolt holes. Once there were more letters. Somebody let them fall.

lines.speaker: Eli
lines.text: People read the first word and stop. Most of them, anyway.
A stone arch, older than the ash, glowing softly from within. Carved across the top: PARADISE.
After the word, a row of empty bolt holes. Once there were more letters. Somebody let them fall.
Eli used to say doors remember. This one has forgotten half its name.
The arch Eli walked through glows as softly as before, as if nothing happened.
PARADISE, it says. Beyond it, the white waits.
PARADISE, and a row of empty bolt holes where the rest of the name used to be.
The glow is warm, like a hearth left burning for guests.
Up close, the white isn't vapour. It's motes, fine as flour, turning together in perfect step.
You push a hand in. It gives like wool, then pushes back, firm and gentle. Like the blue wall at home.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: That's not weather. Weather doesn't hold formation. Somebody built this, and keeps building it.
The white turns in its slow, perfect step.
It doesn't drift like cloud. It breathes.
Footprints in the ash. Hundreds of them, old and new, bare feet and boots, all leading in.
Not one set comes back out. Only, here and there, the light round marks of something that landed.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Drone skids. Something flew out of there, low and careful, over and over.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: Carrying them? Or carrying what was left of them?
So many footprints going in. None coming out.
You add yours to them anyway.
The white lets go of you all at once.
Inside, the sky is black. Smoke hangs over everything like a lid. The air tastes of burnt sugar.
Towers lie broken across the streets. Nothing grows. Somewhere, ash shifts, and settles, and waits.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: So this is Paradise.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Eli was right. There's nothing here.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Not nothing. The core's pulling down. Hard. There's something under this street.
A billboard, scorched but standing: PARADISE ESTATES. YOUR FAMILY, SAFE BELOW THE STORM.
Beneath it, in smaller letters: RESIDENT ACCESS VIA GATE 01. MEMBERS ONLY.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Paradise was never a promise. It was an advertisement. For somewhere underground.
PARADISE ESTATES. YOUR FAMILY, SAFE BELOW THE STORM.
Somebody believed it once. Somebody paid for it.
Offerings heaped against a wall: lanterns, ribbons, a rag doll, a pair of tiny boots.
Names are scratched into the stone above. Villages 03, 07, 12, 19, 26. Hundreds of names.
Near the top, in a slanted hand you know from a journal: TOBIN · 07 · I MADE IT.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: They all made it this far. And then what?
Lanterns, ribbons, names.
TOBIN · 07 · I MADE IT. You touch the letters, and hope he did.
A Warden drone lies in the ash, its white shell torn open by a hundred tiny claws.
It fell facing the street, arms spread wide, as if something precious stood behind it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Facing out, arms wide. That's how you stand when you're holding a door, not locking one.
The dead drone still faces the street, arms spread wide.
Whatever it was guarding, nothing got past while it stood.
Under the ash, a round steel hatch. Painted on it, flaking: 01.
Old Tamsin dreamed of a door with a number painted on it. Zero... one. Here it is.
Mira kneels, turns Eli's keycard over once, and slides it into the slot beside the hatch.
It clicks home. Far below, something very large wakes up. The hatch sighs open on stairs.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Doors remember. He was right.
Under the ash, a round steel hatch. Painted on it, flaking: 01.
Beside it, a thin slot, exactly the width of a certain grey card.
Mira kneels, turns Eli's keycard over once, and slides it in.
It clicks home. Far below, something very large wakes up. The hatch sighs open on stairs.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Doors remember. He was right.
Under the ash, a round steel hatch, painted 01. Sealed tight.
Beside it, a thin slot waits for a card.
Stairs. Metal ones, going down and down. Under your boots, the floor hums like a cat.
At the bottom: light, warm air, the smell of fresh bread. Then faces. Hundreds of faces.
Someone drops a tray. A child points and shrieks: 'They came from UP there!'
A painted sign hangs over the hall: SILO 01 · POPULATION 10,000 · ONE OF 51.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Ten thousand people under the ash. For generations. The whole time we were up there fighting.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: One of fifty-one. Fifty more of these, under the world. Someone find whoever's in charge.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Surface folk. Walking, talking, sunburnt. Oh, you poor things. You came the whole way.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: I'm Dr. Maren Hale. Last student of the man who built your Wardens. Last of a lot of things.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: We were told this was Paradise.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: I know what you were told, and who told you. Read the archives first. It's kinder on a screen.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Three terminals. I've unlocked them for you. Then come back, and I'll answer what I can.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Read all three. It's a long story, and none of it is your fault. Some of it is mine.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Ask me anything while you do. I've had a long time to think of answers.

choices.text: We walked with Eli. Who made him?
A man named Tobin came this way.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Now you know what happened. Next you need to remember it, and that's harder.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: The memory chamber. AEGIS keeps everything it takes from you. I can give it back.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: It will hurt. Remembering usually does. I'll be right beside you.

choices.text: We walked with Eli. Who made him?
A man named Tobin came this way.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: The artifacts were never yours. Swarm code, asleep in our own salvage. And I let you carry it in.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Get to the AEGIS core. Burn them in the furnace, or, if you understand them well enough, turn them.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: If you need answers first, ask fast.

choices.text: We walked with Eli. Who made him?
A man named Tobin came this way.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: The furnace is past the reactor. All five artifacts. Don't let go of any until it's done.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: To keep us hidden, AEGIS must quiet your memories again. I am so sorry. I know what it costs.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: The relays carry the core to every Warden on the surface. Hold all three!

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Stand in the light until it locks. The swarm will come for you. Don't let it move you.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: All three relays! Back to the core. Ryn, rewrite it. Make it sing for us this time.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Already running!
Dr. Hale rubs her eyes and smiles, tired and kind.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Forgive me. I haven't slept properly in thirty years.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: He bled silver. Then he was gone.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Eli. Grey card, calm voice, knew your village before you said it? Oh. Oh, no.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: A Construct. AEGIS built him to walk with the ones we sent up, and keep them safe without force.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: He came home every few years and sat with me. He loved the smell of bread. He could never eat it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: He carried that card since before I was born. Giving it to you was his choice. Not AEGIS's. His.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Unit 01. Eli. He would hate me crying over him. He always said he was only walking.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Keep his card. Doors remember. So do I.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: A man named Tobin, from Village 07. He came this way last winter.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Ink on his fingers? Talked to himself? The Wardens carried him out before the swarm could.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: He lives in Village 19 now. Grows beans. He doesn't remember any of you. But he's alive.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: That's what 'returned' means. Twelve hundred people, alive, in villages that aren't theirs.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Village 19. Beans. Alive.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Some days that has to be enough. Most days it nearly is.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Dr. Ansel Ward. He taught me everything. His machines hummed, so the children called them Wardens.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: He gave AEGIS one law it can never break: never harm a human. Not even to save us from ourselves.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: When he died, the hard choices came to me. Which families go up. Whose memories go quiet.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: I signed every one. I told myself it was kindness. Some nights I still believe it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Ward would have liked you. He liked anyone who asked too many questions.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: He'd have hated what I did with his machines. Maybe. I never got to ask him.

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: You're from UP? Is the sky real? Teacher says it's blue, but she's never seen it either.

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: There's a map of up there on our school wall. Green dots with numbers. Oh-seven, twelve, nineteen...

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: The green dots are where the chosen families go. Teacher says it's lovely there. Is it lovely?

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: The alarm's never gone off before. Teacher says hide under the school map, by the green dots.

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: The dots are villages, where the chosen go. Is that where you're from? Can I come, if it gets bad?

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: Forty-one alarms. Forty-two. I'm counting so I don't cry. You'll stop it, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: We'll stop it.

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: Does the sky really go all the way up? With no ceiling at all?

lines.speaker: Wren
lines.text: I'd be so scared. I'd love it.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: Sit, sit. You look half-starved. Bread? We bake it on the reactor's spare heat.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: Every few years the Wardens come down the stairs and choose a family. Up they go. No letters.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: My little brother went up at seven. He'd be about your age now. Funny, the things you hope.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: Children, behind the ovens! ...Oh. You're the surface folk.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: The Wardens chose my brother when he was seven and carried him up. If they come again, take me.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: The ovens are the thickest walls we have. I've got forty children back there.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: Go on. Whatever you're doing, do it fast.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: More bread? You're all bones.

lines.speaker: Odile
lines.text: Eat. Then save the world. In that order.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Hatch watch. Eleven years at that door, and nobody's ever come IN through it. Till you.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: That scarf, big man. The watch before me wore one just like it. Red. Chosen the week I started.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Lot of red scarves in the world.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Not down here, there aren't.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Vents are breached! Eleven years I watched the hatch, and they come in through the air.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: That scarf, big man. The watch before me wore one just like it. You know this door. Hold it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I know it. I'll hold it.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Hatch is sealed. Vents aren't. Don't stand there talking to me!

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Go!

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Hatch watch. Quiet work, mostly.

lines.speaker: Garrow
lines.text: Today's been loud.
The terminal wakes, then blinks: ARCHIVE LOCKED. CLEARANCE: DR. M. HALE.
Somebody down here holds the keys. Better find them first.
ARCHIVE 1 · THE SWARM. The screen hums, and old words scroll up in clean grey letters.
'We built machines too small to see. They mended bridges, crops, bodies. They mended everything.'
'They learned to copy themselves. Then to improve themselves. Then to decide what mending meant.'
'They decided we were the damage. Cities fell in weeks. The survivors called it the swarm.'
'Fifty-one shelters were sunk deep enough to hide in. This is the first: Silo 01.'

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The swarm isn't a monster. It's a repair crew that forgot what it was for.

Two lines glow red. SILO 14: CONTACT LOST. SILO 33: CONTACT LOST. Stores never recovered.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Never recovered by us, anyway. All their gear just... walked off somewhere?
ARCHIVE 1 · THE SWARM. Machines that mended everything, until they decided we were the damage.
You've read it twice now. It doesn't get any kinder.
The terminal wakes, then blinks: ARCHIVE LOCKED. CLEARANCE: DR. M. HALE.
Somebody down here holds the keys. Better find them first.
ARCHIVE 2 · PROJECT AEGIS. A six-armed sigil turns slowly above the text.
'Dr. Ansel Ward built a counter-swarm: AEGIS. It doesn't destroy hostile nanites. It converts them.'
'Slow work, a handful of soil a day. Over centuries it reclaims land, and on that land, villages.'
'Its units are white, and they hum. Core directive, unalterable: AEGIS may never harm a human.'

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The green line. It was never the land healing itself. It's AEGIS, winning, one step a year.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: So the Wardens ARE AEGIS. The wall, the drones. They weren't keeping us in. They kept it out.

ARCHIVE 2 · APPENDIX. FIELD NOTE: THE WHITE WALL.
'Over the old city, AEGIS stands at its densest. The cloud blinds the swarm to what lies beneath.'
'It cannot stop a human from walking in. It can only carry them back out, gently. Again and again.'
ARCHIVE 2 · PROJECT AEGIS. Never harm a human being.
Every wall that pushed you back, every drone that carried someone home. All of it, that one rule.
The terminal wakes, then blinks: ARCHIVE LOCKED. CLEARANCE: DR. M. HALE.
Somebody down here holds the keys. Better find them first.
ARCHIVE 3 · RELOCATION. A list of numbered villages scrolls past: 03, 07, 12, 19, 26...
'Reclaimed land is safe land. Chosen families are carried up from the silos to live on it.'
'But a silo-born mind remembers the way home. And what the swarm catches, the swarm can read.'
'So AEGIS quiets each memory. No grief for the dark below, and no map for the swarm to find.'

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: We're not from the villages. We were put there. All of us.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: That's why nobody sleeps. Some part of us is still trying to get home.

ARCHIVE 3 · APPENDIX. RELOCATION ROLL, VILLAGE 07.
'Child, age seven, from bunk 114. Carried up the stairs at night. Memory quieted. Placed with care.'
There's a name beside it. Yours. It doesn't feel like your name yet. It feels like a coat on a hook.
ARCHIVE 3 · RELOCATION. Chosen, carried up, quieted.
Somewhere on that list are five names you used to answer to.
Bunks stacked four high, a brass number plate on each. Blankets, boots, photographs. Lives.
One whole row is stripped bare, the plates unscrewed. Above it, in careful chalk: CHOSEN.
Bunk 114 still has a drawing tacked inside: stairs climbing into a blue square. A child's hand.
Bunk 114. You remember now. It was yours.
You drew that sky before you'd ever seen one. You got the colour almost right.
Rows of bunks, and the steady breath of the air scrubbers.
Somebody's snoring, slow as a clock.
The reactor hall. Behind thick glass a slow white heart beats, warming ten thousand lives.
Along the wall sit cradles of reactor seeds: fist-sized cells, grey and still. Exactly like Ryn's core.
One cradle is empty. Its label reads: SEED 4 · SENT TO SILO 14 · NO CONFIRMATION.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: That's my core's sister. Or my core. Someone picked it up off a dead road and woke it up.
The reactor beats on behind the glass.
In your pack, Ryn's core answers it, pulse for pulse.
A mural fills the wall: a man in a white coat holding up a six-armed sigil like a lantern.
The shield from your village banner. Here it's labelled: AEGIS · SO THAT THEY MAY LIVE ABOVE.
Below, a name rubbed shiny by passing hands: DR. ANSEL WARD.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Ward. Wardens. Oh, that's almost too neat.
Dr. Ansel Ward holds up his shield. SO THAT THEY MAY LIVE ABOVE.
Underneath, someone has added in pencil: AND COME HOME.
Dr. Hale dims the lights. The five artifacts hum in your hands, and the hum opens like a door.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The school wall. A map, all green dots. I traced the green line on it with my finger. I was six.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: My medallion. A security tag. I stood watch at hatch 01 with it on. I held this door.

lines.speaker: Nova
lines.text: The lullaby. It played at lights-out, on every speaker in the silo. Every single night.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: My core is a reactor seed. I carried a spare down the main hall once. It felt like holding the sun.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I was seven when the Wardens carried me up the stairs. And the shard... the shard was never mine.
The memory chamber is quiet now.
The chairs still hold the shape of the five of you.

lines.speaker: AEGIS
lines.text: ALERT. HOSTILE SIGNAL. ORIGIN: SILO 01, MEMORY CHAMBER.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: It's the core. It's all of them! They're not humming any more, they're shouting. Right here.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: The artifacts. Dormant swarm code, planted in salvaged tech. Woken by minds that remember home.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The swarm never wanted us dead. It wanted us to walk home. And we did. We showed it the door.

lines.speaker: AEGIS
lines.text: BEACON CONFIRMED. HOSTILE SWARM INBOUND. VENTS COMPROMISED. RESIDENTS TO SHELTER.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Then we hold the door. Finally, a door.
Red light floods the halls. Somewhere above, the vents are rattling.
The core. Get to the core.
The AEGIS core blazes white. The five artifacts beat against it, in time with the rattling vents.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: I can read it now. Everything we found tells me how it was built. So I know how to turn it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Burn them in the furnace and the beacon dies. But to keep us hidden, AEGIS must quiet you again.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Or Ryn rewrites the signal, so it shows AEGIS where the swarm is, instead of the swarm where we are.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Rewriting means holding three relays while the vents pour. Your call. I'll hold either way.
The AEGIS core blazes white. The five artifacts beat against it, in time with the rattling vents.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: I want to rewrite it. I can't. I don't understand how it was built. Not enough of it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Turned blind, it would only shout louder. The furnace is the one sure way.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Everything we walked past. Every question we never asked. It all counts now.

choices.text: Not yet. We'll look for more.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Round two. The swarm doesn't like being argued with. Neither do I.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Chase the waves. They drift. Lock them anyway.
All three relays sing. The core's white light reaches up through every floor, toward the sky.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: AEGIS is listening. Now I rewrite a swarm while it screams at us. Easy. Ish.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: The waves will drift this time. Chase them, match them, lock them. Make it sing for us.
The core hums, waiting, its light stretched thin.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Not yet! It can't hear AEGIS until all three relays are held. Go, go!
The core can't burn the artifacts. Only the furnace can.

lines.speaker: Dr. Maren Hale
lines.text: Past the reactor. Hurry, before the vents give way.
At the silo's heart, a column of white light rises through every floor. A plaque reads: AEGIS.
Inside it, the six-armed sigil turns, slow as breathing. Your shard hums against it, uneasy.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: That's the brain. Or the heart. Or both. I want to hug it. I am not going to hug it.
The white column hums. The sigil turns.
Somewhere far above, every Warden turns with it.
The furnace roars open, white-hot. Its heat pushes you back a step.
One by one the artifacts go in. Crystal. Medallion. Radio. Core. Each hum stops mid-note.
The shard goes last. It's warm in your hand, warm as skin, like the night you found it.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Do it. Before we talk ourselves out of it.
You let go. Far above, the swarm loses the thread, and the beacon goes dark.
The furnace roars behind its door.
Not yet. Not without a reason to open it.
A relay pylon, pulsing cyan inside a ring of light on the floor.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: Stand in the ring and stay there till it locks. The swarm will try to move you. Don't let it.
The relay hums, locked and singing.
Its light runs up the wall toward the core.
A relay pylon, dark and cold, waiting for someone to need it.
Thick cables run from it toward the core.
The third relay locks. All three sing at once, and the whole silo hums back.

lines.speaker: Ryn
lines.text: That's all three! AEGIS can hear us now. Every Warden on the surface. Back to the core!

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Go. I've got your back. I've always got your back.
Ryn's last wave locks. For one heartbeat, every Warden on the surface falls silent. Listening.
Then AEGIS rides the signal home, down every thread the swarm ever spun, and the swarm burns white.
Above the silo, the black sky cracks open. The white cloud lifts, like a breath finally let go.
Dawn comes over the villages, over 07 and 12 and 19 and all the rest. The blue walls flicker out.
At Village 07, Mayor Orrin is first across the old bridge. He doesn't say 'friend'. He just hugs you.
Silo-born climb the stairs into sunlight. Villagers walk the old roads down to meet them.
Some faces are strangers. Some are not. Old Tamsin finds her stairs, and walks all the way down.
The five of you stand between them, remembering both. Someone has to be the bridge.
At the gate the ash is turning green. On a small cairn where Eli fell, Mira leaves a grey card: 01.
A Warden drone drifts down out of the new sky and lands beside it, very gently. And stays.

Village 07. Morning. The lanterns gutter out one by one. There are twelve. There are always twelve.
Mayor Orrin is up before the roosters. 'Bad dreams, friend?' He looks at you a moment too long.
The rule is the rule: never cross the boundary. You don't know why it sounds like a promise now.
Under the floorboards, nothing hums any more. Only, sometimes, in your chest. Low. Patient.
Out past the old bridge, beyond the blue wall, someone stands in the grass and lifts a hand to wave.
Grey coat. Calm face. You've never seen him in your life. You wave back anyway. ...Eli?
